# Comprehensive Feature Specification

## Executive Summary

This is an extremely detailed description designed to test the parsing capabilities of the system when dealing with large text content. In real-world scenarios, developers and product owners often create extensive descriptions with multiple sections, code examples, diagrams, and detailed requirements.

## Background and Context

The current system lacks the ability to handle complex user authentication scenarios. We need to implement a comprehensive solution that supports multiple authentication methods, integrates with existing identity providers, and maintains backward compatibility with legacy systems.

### Current State

- Basic username/password authentication only
- No support for SSO or OAuth
- Session management is primitive
- Security vulnerabilities identified in audit

### Desired Future State

- Multi-factor authentication support
- Integration with corporate SSO (SAML, OAuth2, OIDC)
- Modern session management with JWT
- Enhanced security posture
- Improved user experience

## Detailed Requirements

### Functional Requirements

#### FR1: OAuth2 Authentication

The system shall support OAuth2 authentication with the following providers:

- Google OAuth2
- Microsoft Azure AD
- GitHub OAuth
- Generic OAuth2 providers (configurable)

**Acceptance Criteria:**

```gherkin
Given a user on the login page
When they click "Sign in with Google"
Then they are redirected to Google OAuth consent screen
And upon successful authentication
Then they are logged into the application
And their profile is created or updated
```

#### FR2: SAML Integration

The system shall support SAML 2.0 authentication for enterprise SSO:

- Support for multiple SAML identity providers
- Configurable SP metadata
- Automatic user provisioning from SAML assertions
- Group/role mapping from SAML attributes

**Technical Details:**

```xml
<saml:AttributeStatement>
  <saml:Attribute Name="email">
    <saml:AttributeValue>user@example.com</saml:AttributeValue>
  </saml:Attribute>
  <saml:Attribute Name="groups">
    <saml:AttributeValue>admins</saml:AttributeValue>
    <saml:AttributeValue>developers</saml:AttributeValue>
  </saml:Attribute>
</saml:AttributeStatement>
```

#### FR3: Multi-Factor Authentication

The system shall support the following MFA methods:

1. **Time-based One-Time Passwords (TOTP)**
   - Google Authenticator compatible
   - QR code enrollment
   - Backup codes

2. **SMS-based OTP**
   - Configurable SMS provider
   - Rate limiting
   - International number support

3. **Email-based OTP**
   - Fallback option
   - Configurable validity period

4. **Hardware Security Keys**
   - WebAuthn/FIDO2 support
   - USB and NFC keys
   - Biometric authenticators

### Non-Functional Requirements

#### NFR1: Performance

- Authentication response time < 500ms (p95)
- Support 10,000 concurrent authentication requests
- Token refresh < 100ms (p95)

#### NFR2: Security

- Compliance with OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet
- Password hashing using Argon2id
- Automatic session timeout after 30 minutes inactivity
- Session invalidation on logout
- Protection against:
  - Brute force attacks (rate limiting)
  - Session fixation
  - CSRF attacks
  - XSS attacks (secure cookie settings)

#### NFR3: Reliability

- 99.9% uptime SLA
- Graceful degradation if OAuth providers unavailable
- Automatic failover for authentication services
- Database replication for session storage

#### NFR4: Scalability

- Horizontal scaling capability
- Stateless authentication (JWT-based)
- Distributed session storage (Redis cluster)
- Load balancer compatible

## Technical Approach

### Architecture Overview

```
┌─────────────────┐
│   Frontend      │
│   Application   │
└────────┬────────┘
         │
         │ HTTPS
         ▼
┌─────────────────┐      ┌──────────────┐
│   API Gateway   │◄────►│   OAuth2     │
│   + Auth        │      │   Providers  │
│   Middleware    │      └──────────────┘
└────────┬────────┘
         │              ┌──────────────┐
         ├─────────────►│   SAML IDP   │
         │              └──────────────┘
         │
         ▼
┌─────────────────┐      ┌──────────────┐
│   Auth Service  │◄────►│   Redis      │
│                 │      │   (Sessions) │
└────────┬────────┘      └──────────────┘
         │
         │
         ▼
┌─────────────────┐
│   PostgreSQL    │
│   (Users, MFA)  │
└─────────────────┘
```

### Technology Stack

- **Backend**: Python 3.11+ with FastAPI
- **Authentication**: Authlib (OAuth2/OIDC), python3-saml (SAML)
- **Session Management**: Redis with redis-py
- **Password Hashing**: argon2-cffi
- **Database**: PostgreSQL 15+ with asyncpg
- **MFA**: pyotp (TOTP), twilio (SMS)
- **Frontend**: React 18+ with TypeScript

### Database Schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE users (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    password_hash VARCHAR(255),
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    last_login TIMESTAMPTZ,
    is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,
    email_verified BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE
);

CREATE TABLE oauth_accounts (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    provider VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    provider_user_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    access_token TEXT,
    refresh_token TEXT,
    expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    UNIQUE(provider, provider_user_id)
);

CREATE TABLE mfa_settings (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    method VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    secret TEXT,
    phone_number VARCHAR(20),
    is_enabled BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Foundation (Sprint 1)

- Set up project structure
- Configure development environment
- Implement basic user model
- Set up PostgreSQL and Redis
- Create authentication middleware

### Phase 2: OAuth2 (Sprint 2-3)

- Implement OAuth2 client library integration
- Create provider configuration system
- Implement Google OAuth flow
- Add Microsoft Azure AD support
- Implement GitHub OAuth
- Add generic OAuth2 provider support

### Phase 3: SAML (Sprint 4-5)

- Set up SAML service provider
- Implement metadata generation
- Create assertion consumer service
- Add attribute mapping
- Implement group/role synchronization

### Phase 4: MFA (Sprint 6-7)

- Implement TOTP enrollment and verification
- Add backup codes generation
- Integrate SMS provider
- Implement WebAuthn support
- Create MFA settings UI

### Phase 5: Security & Testing (Sprint 8)

- Security audit and penetration testing
- Performance testing and optimization
- Load testing (10K concurrent users)
- Documentation completion
- Deployment preparation

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests

- Individual authentication methods
- Token generation and validation
- Password hashing and verification
- MFA code generation and validation
- Coverage target: ≥90%

### Integration Tests

- End-to-end OAuth flows
- SAML authentication workflows
- MFA enrollment and verification
- Session management
- Coverage target: ≥80%

### Security Tests

- Automated vulnerability scanning
- Manual penetration testing
- OWASP Top 10 verification
- Session security tests

### Performance Tests

- Load testing with k6
- Stress testing authentication endpoints
- Database query optimization
- Redis performance validation

## Risks and Mitigation

### Risk 1: OAuth Provider Downtime

**Impact**: High
**Probability**: Medium
**Mitigation**: 
- Implement fallback to email/password
- Clear error messages
- Status page integration
- Monitoring and alerts

### Risk 2: SAML Configuration Complexity

**Impact**: Medium
**Probability**: High
**Mitigation**:
- Comprehensive documentation
- Configuration wizard
- Test mode for debugging
- Expert consultation available

### Risk 3: Performance Degradation

**Impact**: High
**Probability**: Low
**Mitigation**:
- Extensive load testing
- Redis clustering
- Database indexing optimization
- CDN for static assets

## Success Metrics

- Authentication success rate > 99.5%
- Average authentication time < 300ms
- Zero critical security vulnerabilities
- User satisfaction score > 4.5/5
- Adoption rate > 80% within 3 months

## Dependencies

- PROJ-50: User management system upgrade
- PROJ-75: Redis cluster setup
- PROJ-82: Database migration framework
- External: Corporate SSO provider configuration

## Documentation Requirements

- API documentation (OpenAPI/Swagger)
- Administrator guide for SSO configuration
- End-user authentication guide
- Security best practices document
- Runbook for operations team

## Acceptance Criteria

✅ All authentication methods functional and tested
✅ Security audit passed with no critical issues
✅ Performance benchmarks met
✅ Documentation complete
✅ Deployment runbook validated
✅ Monitoring and alerting configured
✅ Rollback plan tested
✅ Training completed for operations team

## References

- [OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authentication_Cheat_Sheet.html)
- [OAuth 2.0 RFC 6749](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6749)
- [SAML 2.0 Technical Overview](http://docs.oasis-open.org/security/saml/Post2.0/sstc-saml-tech-overview-2.0.html)
- [WebAuthn Specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/webauthn/)
- [NIST Digital Identity Guidelines](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/)

## Appendix A: Configuration Example

```yaml
authentication:
  providers:
    oauth2:
      google:
        client_id: "${GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID}"
        client_secret: "${GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET}"
        redirect_uri: "https://app.example.com/auth/callback/google"
      
      microsoft:
        client_id: "${MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID}"
        client_secret: "${MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET}"
        tenant_id: "${MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID}"
        redirect_uri: "https://app.example.com/auth/callback/microsoft"
    
    saml:
      corporate_sso:
        entity_id: "https://app.example.com"
        acs_url: "https://app.example.com/auth/saml/acs"
        idp_metadata_url: "${IDP_METADATA_URL}"
        attribute_mapping:
          email: "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress"
          groups: "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/claims/Group"
  
  session:
    provider: "redis"
    timeout: 1800
    secure_cookie: true
    same_site: "strict"
  
  mfa:
    enabled: true
    required_for_admins: true
    totp:
      issuer: "Example App"
      digits: 6
      period: 30
    sms:
      provider: "twilio"
      from_number: "${TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER}"
```

## Appendix B: Error Codes

- AUTH_001: Invalid credentials
- AUTH_002: Account locked
- AUTH_003: MFA required
- AUTH_004: MFA code invalid
- AUTH_005: OAuth provider error
- AUTH_006: SAML assertion invalid
- AUTH_007: Session expired
- AUTH_008: Insufficient permissions

This description intentionally contains extensive detail to test system limits and parsing capabilities.
